In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing theorem''' is an extension of the [[Kodaira vanishing theorem]], on the vanishing of coherent [[cohomology group]]s, to [[logarithmic pair]]s, proved independently by [[Eckart Viehweg|Viehweg]]<ref>{{Citation | authorlink=Eckart Viehweg | last1=Viehweg | first1=Eckart | title=Vanishing theorems | url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=PPN243919689_0335&DMDID=dmdlog4 |mr=667459 | year=1982 | journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]] | issn=0075-4102 | volume=335 | pages=1–8}}</ref> and [[Yujiro Kawamata|Kawamata]]<ref>{{Citation | authorlink=Yujiro Kawamata | last1=Kawamata | first1=Yujiro | title=A generalization of Kodaira-Ramanujam's vanishing theorem | doi=10.1007/BF01456407 |mr=675204 | year=1982 | journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] | issn=0025-5831 | volume=261 | issue=1 | pages=43–46| s2cid=120101105 }}</ref> in 1982.

The theorem states that if ''L'' is a [[Iitaka dimension#Big line bundles|big]] [[nef line bundle|nef]] [[line bundle]] (for example, an [[ample line bundle]]) on a complex projective manifold with [[canonical bundle|canonical line bundle]] ''K'',
then the coherent cohomology groups ''H''<sup>''i''</sup>(''L''⊗''K'') vanish for all positive ''i''.
